transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… yes. Um, I’m not sure if this is the right sort of thing to bring here, but it’s been getting hard to manage. I’m a teacher, and when I see myself on lesson videos, I can’t stop noticing one side of my face. It looks crooked to me, sort of swollen-looking, and once I see it, I can’t really unsee it.

I know that might sound a bit… vain, maybe, and I don’t want to make too much of it, but I keep feeling like the students, parents, and other staff must be staring at that instead of listening to what I’m saying. It’s become really distracting for me.
Do you find yourself avoiding situations where you might be observed or feel self-conscious, like teaching in front of a class or even talking with colleagues?

I’m not sure I’d say I avoid things, exactly… I mean, I still go in and teach, and I try to be professional about it. Talking with colleagues is mostly okay, I think.

I suppose I do feel quite self-conscious when I know I’m being watched, or if there’s a camera involved. But I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself thinking about this concern with your face for a significant amount of time each day—like more than an hour—or does it keep coming up in your mind even when you don’t want it to?

Yes… I think it does keep coming up, even when I’m trying not to let it. I don’t want to overstate it, but once I’ve seen that crooked, swollen-looking side of my face on the lesson videos, it sort of stays with me.

I’ll be teaching or thinking about parents or other staff seeing the recording, and I keep wondering if they’re noticing it instead of what I’m actually saying. It’s embarrassing to admit, but I can’t really switch it off.
Would you say that the part of your face you’re concerned about looks significantly flawed to you, even though others might not seem to notice it or mention it?

Yes… I think so. I mean, to me it looks really obvious, like one side of my face is crooked or sort of swollen-looking, especially on the lesson videos.

I know other people don’t really say anything, so maybe I’m making too much of it… but once I notice it, I can’t stop seeing it. And then I start feeling like the students, or parents, or other staff must be looking at that instead of listening to what I’m saying. Is that… does that make sense?
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to cover it up—because of your concern about how your face looks?

Yes… I suppose I do, a bit. Mostly around anything recorded or on camera.

Before I post a lesson video, or if I’m joining a parent conference, I’ll keep adjusting the camera angle and replaying little clips to check how my face looks. Sometimes I catch myself sort of covering part of my face with my hand, or positioning myself so that side doesn’t show as much.

I don’t want to make it sound ridiculous, but I have re-recorded whole sections because of it. More than once, really. And then I end up losing time I should be using for prep, or I’m late getting to the next class. I know that probably isn’t ideal.

When you look in the mirror or at videos of yourself, do you think that what you’re seeing is something that most people would not even notice, or do you feel like it's something that others probably see and judge as you do?

I want to say most people probably wouldn’t notice… because that sounds more reasonable, doesn’t it? But honestly, when I see it in the mirror or especially on the lesson videos, it feels so obvious to me.

It’s that crooked, kind of swollen-looking side of my face, and once I’ve seen it I can’t unsee it. Then I start thinking the students, parents, or other staff must be staring at that instead of listening to anything I’m saying. I know that may not be fair, but in the moment it really feels like they can see it the way I do.

When you're worried about how that side of your face looks, is it more about how you think others are seeing you in that moment, or is it more about how you see yourself and how much it bothers you regardless of what others may or may not think?

I think… it’s both, but maybe it starts with how I see it.

Like, I’ll notice that side of my face looking crooked or swollen on a lesson video, and then I just can’t stop seeing it. And once that happens, I immediately start thinking, “Well, the students must be seeing it too,” or parents, or other staff… like they’re staring at that instead of listening to what I’m saying.

I know that probably sounds a bit much. I don’t want to seem vain or anything. It just feels really hard to ignore once I’ve noticed it.
If you were completely alone, with no one watching or evaluating you, would you still find yourself bothered by how that side of your face looks?

Yes… I think I would, honestly.

I mean, I’d like to say it’s only because of other people seeing it, because that feels a bit more understandable. But even if I’m completely alone, once I notice that side of my face looking crooked or swollen, especially on a video, I can’t really stop seeing it.

Then my mind does go to students or parents or staff staring at it, but the first part is just me getting stuck on it myself. If that makes sense.
